summary: Eight findings: all seven earlier findings preserved, plus a publication-specific bibliography misprint E8. E1–E4 have author or published corrections; E8 is already correct in the author/arXiv copy; no earlier correction for E5–E7 was located. Added version-specific locators, source hashes and a rigorous polynomial-dilation repair of the semilocal lifting step. No independent-review verdict is asserted.

sourceIssues.printed: Consequently, by [BouAC, Chapitre IX, Section 3, numéro 3, Théorème 1], the thickening ε_z := Spec_{O_{C_{k_m}}}(O_{C_{k_m}}/I_z²) is isomorphic to Spec(k_z[u_z]/(u_z²)).
sourceIssues.correction: The Cohen-structure isomorphism need not be an isomorphism of k_m-schemes when k_m is imperfect, and the construction of j needs one. For imperfect (hence infinite) k_m, embed each ε_z in A¹_{k_m} by the geometric presentation theorem [CTHK97, Theorem 3.1.1] applied in C^sm_{k_m}, and make the images disjoint by translations t ↦ t + α with α ∈ k_m. For perfect k_m the printed argument stands.
sourceIssues.reason: Example: k_m = F_p(s), C = A¹_{k_m}, z = V(t^p − s), u = t^p − s. The p-th powers in O/I_z² = k_m[t]/(u²) lie in k_m^p[t^p] = k_m^p[s + u]; writing h ∈ k_m^p[x] by exponents mod p, h(s) = s forces h′(s) = 1, so h(s + u) ≡ s + u. No element has p-th power s, so there is no k_m-algebra map k_z = k_m(s^{1/p}) → O/I_z².

sourceIssues.locator: Cited input: Gille, Le problème de Kneser–Tits, Astérisque 326 (2009), proof of Lemme 4.5(1), p. 54 (page 15 in the errata, which use another pagination); used in the proof of Proposition 8.4, claim (2), author PDF p. 25
sourceIssues.printed: Vu que Z_ℌ(𝔖)/𝔖 est un schéma en groupe réductif dont la fibre spéciale est anisotrope, la théorie de Bruhat–Tits montre que (Z_ℌ(𝔖)/𝔖)(O) = (Z_ℌ(𝔖)/𝔖)(K) [10, 4.6.33]. […] Par ailleurs, il est bien connu que 𝔖(K) ⊂ ℌ(K)^+ [7, prop. 6.11]. (Symbols transcribed; the text layer is garbled.)
sourceIssues.correction: For M = Z_ℌ(𝔖)/𝔖, first prove that M_K is anisotropic. A proper K-parabolic would extend over O by properness of its fixed-type parabolic scheme and specialize to a proper k-parabolic, contradicting special-fiber anisotropy. Henselian smooth lifting and this properness argument give the singleton comparison Par(M)(K) = Par(M)(O) = Par(M)(k), where the whole group is counted as a parabolic; this is not a general assertion that reduction of a smooth proper scheme is injective. For the radical torus T = rad(M), lift a finite Galois splitting extension of k to O; its character-lattice description identifies the cocharacters over K, O and k. Hence T_K has no split subtorus. Together these prove generic anisotropy, and Guo Proposition 6 gives M(O) = M(K). Replace the Borel–Tits reference Proposition 6.11 by Corollaire 6.8.
sourceIssues.reason: Anisotropy of the special fibre does not by itself give M(O) = M(K); the cited Bruhat–Tits result needs M_K anisotropic, which the proof does not establish. The statement of the lemma is unchanged.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Proposition 8.4, claim (2), author PDF p. 25 (the published version p. 24)
sourceIssues.printed: For the claim (2), we first note that the isotropicity assumption implies that G has a proper parabolic subgroup P ⊂ G (see Definition 8.1).
sourceIssues.correction: Definition 8.1 gives a proper parabolic over each local ring, not necessarily over the semilocal base. One sufficient repair, explicitly supplied in the later author survey, strengthens the assumption: each simple factor over its own finite étale base contains G_m (and hence has a fiberwise proper parabolic). This is automatic in the quasi-split application of Theorem 9.1. Alternatively retain the original total-isotropy hypothesis and lift radical points separately at each maximal ideal. The earlier extraction proposes this via a Noetherian reduction and nonzerodivisor denominator clearing; its full proposal is preserved in priorExtractionRepair. A precise replacement is the finite-presentation polynomial dilation argument proved in the companion report: spread an identity-preserving affine-space parameterization to R_s with s outside the chosen maximal ideal and inside the others, clear denominators, and dilate again to kill the finitely many relation coefficients annihilated by powers of s. The resulting map A^d_R → G is identically 1 modulo s and has the desired parameterization after inverting s. Lift Laurent-series coordinates at the chosen residue field and evaluate this map; all other residue components are 1. Applying this to both opposite radicals and the corrected Whitehead factorization proves the needed loop-coset surjectivity. This argument allows zero divisors and needs no Noetherian reduction.
sourceIssues.reason: Example: let Ō be the semilocal ring of A¹_Q at two closed points with residue fields L₁ (cyclic cubic) and L₂ = Q(i), and R = {f ∈ Ō : f(q₁), f(q₂) ∈ Q}, a one-dimensional Noetherian semilocal domain with residue fields Q, Q. Milnor patching of M₆(Ō) with M₂(D) and M₃(H) gives an Azumaya R-algebra A of degree 6, where D is a cubic division algebra split by L₁ and H = (−1,−1)_Q. Here A is split over Frac R, and A_{R_{m₁}} ≅ M₂(D′), A_{R_{m₂}} ≅ M₃(H′), since the patching over each local ring is unique. So G = SL₁(A), simply connected of type A₅, is totally isotropic. An R-parabolic would have a single type, since Dyn(G) is constant, proper on both closed fibres SL₂(D) and SL₃(H). Their parabolics are the flags of reduced dimensions in {3} and in {2, 4} respectively, so there is none. Theorem 9.1 is unaffected: it applies Proposition 8.4 to quasi-split G, which has a Borel over R. The counterexample disproves the asserted global-parabolic inference, not Proposition 8.4 or Theorem 9.1. A concrete choice is L₁ = Q(ζ₇ + ζ₇⁻¹) and D = (L₁/Q, σ, 2): 2 is inert in this cyclic cubic extension, so its valuation prevents 2 from being a norm and D is division. The companion report spells out the conductor patching and the local matrix decompositions.

sourceIssues.priorExtractionRepair: Definition 8.1 gives a proper parabolic only over each local ring of R. Either strengthen the hypothesis for semilocal R as the author later does (each simple factor contains G_m over its own finite étale base; automatic for quasi-split G, the case Theorem 9.1 uses), or keep the hypothesis and work one maximal ideal at a time. For each m take a proper parabolic P_m of G_{R_m} and an opposite P_m^−. For Noetherian R, spread them out over R_g with g a nonzerodivisor of R_red outside m and inside the other maximal ideals, and lift points of R_u(P_m^±)(k_m((t))) to G(R((t))) through coordinates in g^N·R((t)). The lifts are 1 at the other maximal ideals. A limit argument reduces Proposition 8.4 to Noetherian R. The items state this repair.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Corollary 9.6, first sentence, author PDF p. 28 (the published version p. 27)
sourceIssues.printed: Every inner form of SO_n is an SO(E) for a nondegenerate quadratic space E over R of rank n.
sourceIssues.correction: Every twist of SO_n by an SO_n-torsor is an SO(E) for such an E; these are the only twists the argument uses.
sourceIssues.reason: For even n ≥ 4, inner forms also come from central simple algebras with orthogonal involution. Over R = Q (allowed in Theorem 9.1 with O = Q), take H = (−1,−1) and H′ = (−1,3), non-isomorphic quaternion algebras ramified at {2, ∞} and {2, 3}. Then SO(H ⊗ H′, γ ⊗ γ′) ≅ (SL₁(H) × SL₁(H′))/μ₂ is an inner form of split SO₄. It is not an SO(E): for E of trivial discriminant, SO(E) ≅ (SL₁(C) × SL₁(C))/μ₂ with isomorphic factors. For odd n every form is an SO(E), and the proof only twists by H¹(R, SO_n). As a second check, over the real numbers the example has Lie algebra su(2) ⊕ sl₂(R), with one compact and one split simple factor. A four-dimensional real quadratic space gives so(4) (both compact), so(2,2) (both split), or so(3,1) (real simple), never this mixed pair. Thus the Q-example is not SO(E) even without invoking the full classification of algebras with involution. The unrestricted inner-form assertion fails, while pure-inner twisting suffices for the stated corollary.
